jobs.title: Director, International Business Transformation & Strategy Execution (flexible location)
jobs.description:
Chez ABB, nous aidons les industries à être plus efficaces et plus durables, et chaque personne ici contribue à cet impact. Vous aurez le pouvoir d’agir, le soutien nécessaire pour évoluer et la fierté de participer aux résultats que nous créons ensemble. Joignez-vous à nous et contribuez à ce qui fait avancer le monde.

The work model for the role is:
Hybrid

Your Role And Responsibilities

This Director role is a strategic transformation position within ABB's NEMA International division, reporting to the EVP International Sales. The role is pivotal in building a scalable international business platform by strengthening alignment across Regions, Business Lines and functions, removing structural barriers to growth and driving implementation of the Stabilize-Optimize-Scale roadmap. The successful candidate will drive business transformation across regions while building scalable operating foundations, combining expertise in strategy execution, operating-model redesign, business process management, change leadership, and executive influence within a complex global matrix.

The work model for the role is: hybrid ;

The role is contributing to the Motion NEMA Motors division globally.

International travel of approximately 30-40% will be required for the role.

You Will Be Mainly Accountable For

Own and drive the NEMA International transformation roadmap aligned with the Stabilize-Optimize-Scale journey, translating strategy into prioritized initiatives with clear outcomes, milestones and success measures while maintaining visibility of progress and risks to leadership.
Act as senior integrator between NEMA International and Global Business Lines, establishing governance mechanisms and cross-functional commitments that align product, portfolio, and investment priorities with international market requirements while escalating critical dependencies that constrain growth.
Lead resolution of systemic barriers at the interfaces between International Sales, Global Operations, IT, Finance, HR and other supporting functions, converting fragmented issues into prioritized root-cause initiatives with clear accountability and measurable outcomes.
Serve as custodian of the NEMA International target operating model, ensuring organizational accountabilities, governance, processes, technology and capabilities evolve coherently to enable profitable international growth, from stabilization through optimization and scale, while designing the organization for future growth and acquisitions.
Lead an executive-level International Transformation Office that manages the transformation portfolio, governance cadence, dependency view and risk escalation, mobilizing cross-functional workstreams and intervening to resolve ownership gaps, resource constraints or delayed decisions.
Lead adoption of the new international organization and ways of working through change leadership, stakeholder engagement and capability building, while establishing a continuous improvement framework that connects frontline issues to structural business improvements and embeds continuous improvement into leadership accountability.

Qualifications For The Role

Minimum 10 years of progressive experience in business transformation, strategy execution, operating-model design, commercial excellence, enterprise program leadership or management consulting.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Strategy, Operations, Information Systems or a related discipline.
Experience in an internal strategy, transformation, business excellence or consulting role.
Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional transformation across multiple geographies or business units.
Proven ability to align senior stakeholders and functions behind a shared agenda without relying on direct authority.
Experience translating strategy into executable roadmaps, governance, operating mechanisms and measurable outcomes.
Strong business acumen and ability to connect transformation to customer value, growth, margin, cash, productivity and organizational capability.
Excellent executive communication, facilitation and synthesis skills.
Ability to constructively challenge established practices and navigate ambiguity with pace and judgement.
Familiarity with international commercial models, CRM/ERP environments and end-to-end customer processes.
Experience in an industrial, manufacturing, electromechanical or B2B technology environment is an advantage. Recognized transformation, change management, Lean, Six Sigma or program-management certification is a plus.
Fluent English language skills.

More About Us

ABB’s NEMA Motors Division is a marketer, designer and manufacturer that offers Baldor-Reliance® industrial electric motors, primarily in North America. The Division focuses on quality, reliability and efficiency to provide a comprehensive offering of NEMA motors in the market across most industrial segments and applications.

We value people from different backgrounds. Apply today for your next career step within ABB and visit www.abb.com to learn about the impact of our solutions across the globe. #MyABBStory

We look forward to receiving your application (documents submitted in English are appreciated). If you want to discover more about ABB, take another look at our website
www.abb.com
.

Directeur(-trice) transformation des activités internationales et exécution de la stratégie (lieu de travail flexible)

Nos convictions

Chez ABB, nous nous engageons à relever les défis mondiaux. Nos valeurs fondamentales — la bienveillance, le courage, la curiosité et la collaboration —combinées à notre engagement envers la diversité, l’inclusion et l’égalité des chances, sont au cœur de notre volonté de donner à chacun et chacune les moyens de créer des solutions durables.

Écrivez le prochain chapitre de votre histoire chez ABB.

Votre rôle et vos responsabilités

Ce poste de direction est axé sur la transformation stratégique au sein de la division NEMA International d’ABB et relève du vice-président exécutif, ventes internationales. Il joue un rôle essentiel dans la mise en place d’une plateforme d’affaires internationales évolutive en renforçant l’alignement entre les régions, les secteurs d’activité et les fonctions, en éliminant les obstacles structurels à la croissance et en pilotant la mise en œuvre de la feuille de route Stabiliser-Optimiser-Déployer à grande échelle. La personne retenue pilotera la transformation des activités dans les différentes régions tout en établissant des fondations opérationnelles évolutives, en mettant à profit son expertise en exécution de la stratégie, en refonte des modèles opérationnels, en gestion des processus d’affaires, en leadership du changement et en influence auprès de la haute direction dans une structure matricielle mondiale complexe.

Le mode de travail pour ce poste est : hybride;

Ce poste contribue aux activités de la division Moteurs NEMA du secteur Motion à l’échelle mondiale.

Ce poste exige des déplacements internationaux représentant environ 30 à 40 % du temps de travail.

Vos Principales Responsabilités Seront Les Suivantes

Prendre en charge et piloter la feuille de route de transformation de NEMA International, en cohérence avec le parcours Stabiliser-Optimiser-Déployer à grande échelle, en traduisant la stratégie en initiatives prioritaires assorties de résultats, de jalons et de critères de réussite clairs, tout en assurant à la direction une visibilité sur les progrès et les risques.
Agir comme principal point d’intégration entre NEMA International et les secteurs d’activité mondiaux, en établissant des mécanismes de gouvernance et des engagements interfonctionnels qui alignent les priorités en matière de produits, de portefeuille et d’investissements sur les exigences des marchés internationaux, tout en portant à l’attention de la direction les interdépendances critiques qui freinent la croissance.
Piloter la résolution des obstacles systémiques aux interfaces entre les ventes internationales, les opérations mondiales, les TI, les finances, les RH et les autres fonctions de soutien, en regroupant les problèmes isolés en initiatives prioritaires visant leurs causes fondamentales, assorties de responsabilités claires et de résultats mesurables.
Veiller au maintien du modèle opérationnel cible de NEMA International, en s’assurant que les responsabilités organisationnelles, la gouvernance, les processus, les technologies et les capacités évoluent de façon cohérente pour soutenir une croissance internationale rentable, de la stabilisation à l’optimisation, puis au déploiement à grande échelle, tout en concevant l’organisation en fonction de sa croissance et de ses acquisitions futures.
Diriger un bureau de transformation internationale au niveau de la haute direction, responsable du portefeuille de transformation, du rythme de gouvernance, du suivi des interdépendances et du signalement des risques, en mobilisant les chantiers interfonctionnels et en intervenant pour résoudre les lacunes dans l’attribution des responsabilités, les contraintes de ressources ou les retards décisionnels.
Piloter l’adoption de la nouvelle organisation internationale et des nouvelles façons de travailler grâce au leadership du changement, à la mobilisation des parties prenantes et au développement des capacités, tout en établissant un cadre d’amélioration continue qui relie les problèmes de première ligne aux améliorations structurelles des activités et intègre l’amélioration continue aux responsabilités de la direction.

Qualifications Requises Pour Le Poste

Au moins 10 ans d’expérience avec des responsabilités croissantes en transformation des activités, en exécution de la stratégie, en conception de modèles opérationnels, en excellence commerciale, en direction de programmes d’entreprise ou en conseil en gestion.
Baccalauréat ou maîtrise en administration des affaires, en génie, en stratégie, en gestion des opérations, en systèmes d’information ou dans une discipline connexe.
Expérience dans un rôle interne en stratégie, en transformation, en excellence opérationnelle ou en consultation.
Expérience démontrée dans la direction de transformations complexes et interfonctionnelles touchant plusieurs régions géographiques ou unités d’affaires.
Capacité éprouvée à rallier les parties prenantes de la haute direction et les fonctions autour de priorités communes, sans s’appuyer sur une autorité hiérarchique directe.
Expérience dans la traduction de la stratégie en feuilles de route réalisables, en structures de gouvernance, en mécanismes opérationnels et en résultats mesurables.
Solide sens des affaires et capacité à relier la transformation à la valeur pour la clientèle, à la croissance, aux marges, aux flux de trésorerie, à la productivité et aux capacités organisationnelles.
Excellentes aptitudes en communication auprès de la haute direction, en animation et en synthèse.
Capacité à remettre en question les pratiques établies de façon constructive et à évoluer dans l’ambiguïté avec rapidité et discernement.
Connaissance des modèles commerciaux internationaux, des environnements de gestion de la relation client (CRM) et de planification des ressources de l’entreprise (ERP), ainsi que des processus clients de bout en bout.
Une expérience dans un environnement industriel, manufacturier, électromécanique ou de technologies interentreprises (B2B) constitue un atout. Une certification reconnue en transformation, en gestion du changement, en Lean, en Six Sigma ou en gestion de programmes constitue un atout.

jobs.title: Director – Data, Analytics & AI (BFSI)
jobs.description:
We are seeking an accomplished Data & Analytics Leader
to drive enterprise-wide Data, Analytics, and AI transformation initiatives within the Banking, Financial Services, and Insurance (BFSI) sector.

This is a strategic leadership position combining technology consulting, enterprise transformation, business development, and client engagement. The ideal candidate will bring extensive experience in shaping data-led business strategies, building executive relationships, developing strategic opportunities, and delivering measurable business outcomes.
You will work closely with CDOs, CIOs, CAIOs, and senior business stakeholders to define transformation strategies, accelerate AI adoption, and drive business growth.

Key Responsibilities
1. Strategic Leadership & Client Advisory

Build trusted relationships with CDOs, CIOs, CAIOs, and senior business executives.
Advise BFSI clients on enterprise data strategy, analytics transformation, AI adoption, and data modernization.
Lead executive workshops, strategic discussions, and transformation planning sessions.
Translate business challenges into actionable roadmaps and measurable business outcomes.

2. Business Development & Growth

Drive business growth across Data, Analytics, and AI consulting services.
Identify, qualify, and develop strategic opportunities from initial engagement through proposal and closure.
Lead RFP responses, solution development, commercial discussions, and executive presentations.
Build strategic partnerships with technology providers, alliance partners, and consulting practices.
Develop reference customers and establish long-term strategic client relationships.

3. Enterprise Data, Analytics & AI Transformation

Define enterprise data strategies, target architectures, operating models, and governance frameworks.
Drive modernization initiatives across cloud data platforms, data engineering, analytics, and AI.
Guide the adoption of AI, Generative AI, Agentic AI, Machine Learning, and Responsible AI.
Champion modern data platforms, data products, self-service analytics, and decision intelligence.
Ensure solutions meet enterprise requirements for scalability, security, regulatory compliance, and cost optimization.

4. Program & People Leadership

Provide executive oversight across large-scale consulting and transformation engagements.
Establish governance frameworks covering delivery milestones, risks, dependencies, quality, and business outcomes.
Lead and mentor cross-functional teams across consulting, architecture, engineering, analytics, and AI.
Develop reusable frameworks, reference architectures, consulting offerings, and delivery playbooks.
Support leadership development, talent acquisition, succession planning, and capability building.

Required Qualifications & Experience

18+ years of professional experience across Data, Analytics, AI, Technology Consulting, and Enterprise Transformation.
Extensive expertise in Enterprise Data Strategy, Data Architecture, Data Governance, Data Products, and Data Modernization.
Strong understanding of the end-to-end data value chain, including data engineering, integration, ETL/ELT, APIs, DataOps, and platform engineering.
Proven experience leading enterprise Analytics and Business Intelligence initiatives.
Strong knowledge of AI/ML, Generative AI, Agentic AI, MLOps/LLMOps, and Responsible AI.
Experience designing and delivering enterprise-scale solutions using Azure, AWS, GCP, Databricks, Snowflake, and modern data platforms.
Strong understanding of BFSI industry requirements, including regulatory compliance, data privacy, security, risk management, and auditability.
Demonstrated success in consulting, business development, pre-sales, solution architecture, opportunity management, and commercial negotiations.
Experience managing large transformation programs and engaging with C-suite executives.
Proven ability to lead geographically distributed, cross-functional teams.

Education & Certifications
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Business, Data, or a related discipline.
Master's degree or MBA preferred.
Relevant certifications in Cloud, Enterprise Architecture, Data Management, Analytics, AI, Program Management, or Executive Leadership are advantageous.

Leadership Competencies
Executive stakeholder management and relationship building.
Strategic thinking and business development.
Excellent communication, presentation, and influencing skills.
Strong commercial and business acumen.
Enterprise transformation and program governance.
Team leadership, mentoring, and capability development.
High ownership, accountability, and commitment to client success.

jobs.title: DIRECTOR OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

The organization has experienced strong and sustained growth since its founding in 2009 and currently employs nearly 350 people. As part of its strategic plan, the Group aims to accelerate its national and international development.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field. Conditions and Compensation Lacroix Medical Group offers a competitive total compensation package including: Annual salary of $140,000 to $175,000, depending on experience and expertise; 4 weeks of vacation and 4 paid personal days; RRSP+ program with employer contribution; Cell phone allowance; Lacroix Health Credit; and an annual Lacroix gift card. This benefit can be combined with other benefits for personalized medical services.

Business travel expense account for trips outside your usual work area

Join a growing network and become a key player in the future of private medicine in Quebec.

jobs.description:
Location

Brookfield Place - 181 Bay Street

Technology Services

Technology Services (TS) is responsible for delivering all enterprise infrastructure, applications and related end user technology services across all Brookfield business groups.

Brookfield Culture

Brookfield has a unique and dynamic culture. We seek team members who have a long-term focus and whose values align with our Attributes of a Brookfield Leader: Entrepreneurial, Collaborative and Disciplined. jobs.title: Director, Finance

POSITION DESCRIPTION

The Director of Finance is a senior finance leader responsible for the integrity, stewardship, and governance of ESA’s financial operations and financial reporting. This role ensures accurate and timely accounting, compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements, effective cash and balance sheet management, and robust internal controls. They will be responsible for all day-to-day finance operations, including functional responsibility over general accounting, accounts payable, accounts receivable, pension administration, treasury, investments.
The Director of Finance is responsible for audit readiness by ensuring robust policies, systems, and procedures are in place, and by supporting the external audit process as required.
In addition, the Director of Finance will partner with the CFO, senior leadership, and staff to improve progam or process integration to enhance efficiently and effectiveness in achieving program objectives, In relation to any system or process changes, the Director of Finance will collaborate with respective business areas to positively impact design and operational effectiveness in support of business objectives as well as financial and management reporting objectives.
ROLE DESCRIPTION

Financial Accounting and Reporting

· Provide financial and accounting leadership for ESA’s Finance function and business areas. Oversee all accounts, ledgers, and reporting systems and changes thereto, ensuring continued compliance with appropriate GAAP standards and regulatory requirements.
· Design and maintain internal controls and safeguards related to revenue (billings and receipts) and expenditures.
· Oversee the preparation and integrity of monthly, quarterly and annual financial reports in accordance with GAAP.
· Lead the month end and year end close processes, ensuring timeliness, completeness, and accuracy.
· Lead the annual ESA external financial statement audit, including planning, fieldwork and reporting while keeping the CFO apprised of any issues on a timely basis.
· Develop, maintain, and enforce accounting policies, procedures and documentation, maintaining an appropriate audit trail for the external auditors.
· Monitor and assess potential changes in NFPO accounting standards and or gaps in ESA’s accounting policies and provide data driven, clear guidance and recommendations to the CFO.
· Prepare materials for Board/A&IC briefings as part of regular quarterly meetings and/or as required.
Internal Controls, Compliance and Audit

· Design, implement, and maintain a strong internal control framework over financial reporting.
· Ensure compliance with statutory, regulatory, tax, and reporting requirements.
· Act as the primary liaison with external auditors, regulators, and other external stakeholders on accounting and control matters.
· Lead the preparation of audit schedules and support external audit activities through to successful completion.
· Identify, assess, and mitigate financial reporting and operational financial risks.
Accounts payable and Accounts Receivable

· Provide strategic and operational oversight of the accounts payable and accounts receivable functions.
· Ensure efficient, accurate, and timely processing of vendor payments and customer billings and collections.
· Establish and monitor key controls over disbursements, collections, credit management, and reconciliations.
· Oversee the management of aged receivables and support resolution of complex or escalated issues.
· Continuously improve processes to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and compliance.
· Collaborate with cross-functional business areas on review of manual journal entries.
Treasury, Cash Management & Banking

· Oversee daily cash management, bank relationships, and banking structures.
· Ensure appropriate controls over cash receipts, disbursements, and account reconciliations.
· Monitor liquidity and working capital from an operational and control perspective, in alignment with CFO direction.
· Authorize banking arrangements and ensure compliance with signing authorities and delegated limits outlined in the Organizational Authority Registrar.
Investments Oversight (Outsourced Chief Investment Officer Governance)

· Provide financial governance and oversight of ESA’s investment activities managed by an outsourced Chief Investment Officer (OCIO), in accordance with approved investment policies, mandates, and governance frameworks.
· Act as the secondary finance liaison with the OCIO to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of investment‑related financial information and reporting. The CFO is the primary point of contact for investment-related activities.
· Review and assess investment valuations, and accounting treatments prepared under the OCIO’s management for compliance with applicable accounting standards and investment policies.
· Monitor adherence to internal controls related to investment transactions, custody, valuation, and financial disclosures, including controls executed by the OCIO and third‑party service providers.
· Coordinate with the OCIO, custodians, external managers, actuaries (where applicable), and auditors to support audit activities and regulatory reporting related to investments.
· Ensure appropriate investment disclosures are prepared for financial statements
· Support the CFO and relevant board committee by conducting a detailed review of quarterly reports provided by the outsourced Chief Investment Officer (OCIO). This includes assessing the completeness, accuracy, and clarity of reporting related to portfolio performance, asset allocation, valuation methodologies, compliance with the Investment Policy Statement, and key risk exposures.
· Liaise with the OCIO to obtain clarifications, supplemental analysis, or follow‑up information as required to support informed oversight and governance discussions at the committee level.
Pension and Other Post Employment Benefits Accounting

· Oversee accounting, reporting, and compliance related to pension plans and post‑employment benefits.
· Liaise with external actuaries, pension administrators, and external auditors on valuation, disclosures, and funding matters.
· Ensure accurate recording of pension assets, liabilities, expenses, and associated disclosures.
· Support governance and oversight of pension plans in accordance with applicable legislation and policies.
Payroll

· Provide strategic leadership and oversight over ESA’s payroll function, with operational payroll processing executed by senior payroll professionals.
· Set strategic direction, governance standards, and control expectations for payroll operations to ensure accuracy, compliance, and consistency.
· Establish and maintain ESA’s payroll policy.
· Ensure robust internal controls are designed, implemented, and operating effectively over payroll processing, payroll changes, reconciliations, and access management to ESA’s payroll system.
· Oversee payroll accounting and financial integrity, including review of payroll reconciliations and confirmation of accurate recording of payroll‑related expenses, liabilities, and accruals.
· Review and challenge escalated payroll issues, exceptions, or control matters, approving resolution approaches and escalating material risks to the CFO as appropriate.
· Sponsor continuous improvement initiatives related to payroll systems, processes, controls, and reporting to enhance efficiency, risk management, and employee experience.
People Management:

· Lead, mentor, and develop a high performing finance team.
· Set clear performance expectations and foster a culture of accountability, accuracy, and continuous improvement and customer service to cross-functional business units
Other

· Effectively represent the Finance team as a Senior Management Team Member on board committees or internal committees as required.
QUALIFICATIONS

• CPA designation required
• Strong oral and written communication skills.
· At least 10-12 years of progressive experience in accounting and finance.
· Demonstrated experience in financial reporting, internal controls, accounts payable, accounts receivable, investments and pension accounting.
• Experience supervising a team of finance professionals.
• Experience with non-government not for profit accounting and a solid knowledge and
understanding of GAAP and accounting for pensions.
• Analytic, organization, and problem-solving skills for strategic data interpretation.
• Strong emotional intelligence and self-awareness is essential.
• Strong interpersonal and communication skills required to effectively communicate complex
issues to senior leadership.
• The ability to translate complex financial concepts to individuals at all levels including finance and non-finance managers.
• Requires demonstrated listening and negotiating skills and the ability to work effectively with people inside and outside the organization to achieve the required results.

CORE VALUES

One Team. One Redwood

Make Your Own Weather

Obsess over Customer Success

Work the Problem

Be Curious

Own the Outcome

Respect Each Other

YOUR IMPACT

As Director, Customer Education & Documentation, you will lead Redwood's global documentation and customer education practice and rebuild it for an AI-first operating model. You will inherit an established team in Canada and India and reshape it: what the team produces, how it produces it, and how its impact is measured. AI-assisted and agentic content production, a best-in-class docs-as-code platform, in-product guidance through Pendo, and training that shortens time-to-value for new customers and partners are the four pillars of the role.

You are a builder and a player-coach at the system level. You set the strategy, then redesign the workflows, roles, and tooling that deliver it.

Reinvent the Team for AI

Redesign the team's operating model, roles, and skills mix around AI-assisted and agentic content production, moving the team from writing and maintaining content by hand to designing, governing, and validating AI-generated content.
Define which content work is delegated to AI, which stays with human judgment, and how validation is performed. Publish standards for accuracy, review, and provenance that the team follows.
Build and run agentic pipelines for drafting, translation, release-note and change-driven updates, link and quality checks, and content-gap detection.
Reskill current team members, reset role definitions and career paths, and hire selectively for the capabilities the redesigned team requires.
Set measurable productivity and quality targets (cycle time from release to published content, coverage, accuracy, cost per asset) and report results.
Make content structured and machine-readable so that customers, partners, and AI assistants can consume Redwood documentation reliably.

Build Best-in-Class Docs as Code

Own the end-to-end documentation platform strategy: content in version control, authored in Markdown/MDX, built and published through CI/CD, reviewed through pull requests alongside product code.
Lead the migration from legacy authoring tools to a modern docs-as-code platform, including information architecture, content modeling, redirects, search, versioning, and access control.
Embed documentation in the product delivery lifecycle with engineering and Product: docs as a release gate, shared ownership, automated checks, and documentation updates triggered by code and API changes.
Raise API and developer documentation to the standard expected of a platform product, including OpenAPI-driven reference content.
Establish quality, style, localization, and accessibility standards, and instrument documentation with usage and effectiveness analytics.

Drive In-Product Guidance and Onboarding

Own the Pendo guide strategy: in-app walkthroughs, tooltips, announcements, and contextual help that move new users to first value faster and reduce support demand.
Partner with Product, Engineering, and Product Operations on tagging standards, guide governance, and analytics, so guides are resilient to product change and measured against adoption outcomes.
Connect in-product guidance, documentation, and training into one learning experience, so a user reaches the right content in the right place with no hand-offs.

Deliver Training That Changes Customer and Partner Outcomes

Own the global customer education strategy and its delivery through Redwood University (Skilljar): role-based learning paths, certification, instructor-led and on-demand training, and partner and implementation-partner enablement.
Design onboarding programs for new customers and partners that measurably reduce time-to-value, ramp time, and onboarding-related support and services effort.
Use AI to scale course development, localization, personalization, and assessment, while holding a high bar for instructional quality.
Evaluate and, where the case supports it, build scalable and revenue-generating education offerings, including certification and partner programs.
Define and report education outcomes: completion, certification, adoption lift, onboarding time, support deflection, and customer and partner satisfaction.

Lead a Global, Distributed Team

Lead managers and senior individual contributors in Canada and India, with a clear operating rhythm across time zones, shared standards, and consistent quality.
Coach and develop leaders, set expectations, manage performance, and build succession.
Manage the annual plan, budget, and vendor relationships for documentation, learning, and AI tooling, and make build-versus-buy recommendations.
Partner with Product, Engineering, Customer Success, Support, Professional Services, Marketing, and Partner teams to align content and training to the customer journey.
Present strategy, results, risks, and investment needs to senior executives.

10+ years of progressive experience in technical documentation, customer education, developer experience, technical content, or digital adoption for software products, including 5+ years leading managers and distributed teams. Hands-on fluency with AI in content production: you can describe specific workflows where AI generates content, what your team validates, how the tools fail, and how your approach has changed in the past six months. Xplore Inc. is Canada’s fibre, 5G and satellite broadband company for rural living. Xplore is committed to the relentless pursuit of an improved broadband experience for all Canadians. Xplore is building a world-class fibre optic and 5G wireless network to enable innovative broadband services for better every day rural living, for today and future generations.

The Director, Network Development & Operations is the senior leader responsible for turning Xplore’s network architecture into an automated, scalable production network, delivering Core & Transport Network Services at a Tier-1 Telco Gold Standard and ensuring uncompromising reliability, security, and performance from the core to the customer. The role leads the teams accountable for detailed IP engineering, DWDM engineering automation, caching implementation, CI/CD, configuration management, telemetry, and operational tooling.

The Director sets the vision and operating model for network-as-code, ensuring that all IP/MPLS, DWDM, and caching configurations are deployed safely, consistently, and at scale. Under this leadership, the organization builds the automation frameworks, observability pipelines, and operational guardrails that enable high-velocity, low-risk changes across the backbone, reduce manual toil, and strengthen 24×7 operational readiness.

Working in close partnership with Network Architecture & Technology Strategy, the Director ensures that architectural intent is executed through modern DevOps practices, and brings operational insight back into standards, roadmaps, and long-term network evolution. The Director connects network development and operations directly to business outcomes and KPIs — including reliability, speed of change, customer experience, and cost efficiency — and serves as a trusted advisor to senior leadership on operational performance and automation maturity.

Detailed IP, DWDM & Caching Engineering

Own detailed IP engineering across BGP, OSPF, IS-IS, MPLS, segment routing, and routing policy.
Own DWDM configuration automation, including line-system configuration templates, channel provisioning, amplifier and span parameter automation, optical telemetry integration, and operational tooling for DWDM health and performance.

Translate architectural standards into deployable configuration templates and network-as-code artifacts.

Network Automation & CI/CD Pipelines

Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for IP/MPLS/DWDM and caching configuration deployment.
Implement automated testing, validation, and rollback capabilities.
Drive adoption of network-as-code across the Core & Transport domain, ensuring all changes are executed through automated, repeatable workflows.

Telemetry, Observability & Operational Tooling

Own telemetry pipelines, dashboards, and observability tooling for Core & Transport.
Ensure real-time visibility into routing behavior, caching performance and hit ratios, DWDM optical health (OSNR, span performance, and alarms), and capacity and traffic patterns.
Partner with Service Assurance & Observability to integrate signals, alerts, anomaly detection, and automated diagnostics.

Reliability Engineering & Operational Excellence

Implement guardrails, automated checks, and configuration validation to reduce operational risk.
Lead post-incident automation improvements to prevent recurrence.

Partnership with Architecture & Execution of Architectural Intent

Implement the logical connectivity, caching strategy, DWDM design parameters, standards, and principles defined by Network Architecture & Technology Strategy.
Provide feedback loops to Architecture on operational feasibility, automation impacts, and configuration constraints.
Ensure all deployments align with long-range architectural direction and resiliency goals.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Work closely with Network Architecture & Technology Strategy; Carrier Services; Fiber, Fixed Wireless, and Enterprise teams; and NOC, SRE, and Service Assurance.

Financial & Investment Performance

Own the financial and investment performance of the Network Development & Operations portfolio, including capital and operating budgets, business cases, and return-on-investment tracking.
Drive measurable unit cost improvements (e.g., cost per bit, cost per port, cost per subscriber) through automation, standardization, and platform consolidation.
Reduce lifecycle risk by proactively managing hardware and software end-of-life and end-of-support exposure, technical debt, and refresh roadmaps across IP, DWDM, and caching platforms.
Partner with Finance, Architecture, and Procurement to prioritize investments, optimize vendor spend, and align spending with business outcomes.
Report on financial, unit cost, and lifecycle-risk KPIs to senior leadership.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

15+ years of experience in IP engineering, DWDM engineering automation, caching platforms, or DevOps for large-scale network infrastructure.

Technical Expertise

Strong expertise in routing protocols (BGP, OSPF, IS-IS), MPLS/segment routing, and routing policy.
Hands-on experience with DWDM systems, optical telemetry, and line-system configuration.
Experience with caching platforms (CDN nodes, edge caches, content caches).
Experience with automation tools (Ansible, Python, CI/CD frameworks).
Experience with telemetry, observability, and network monitoring systems.

Leadership & Collaboration

Demonstrated ability to lead technical engineering teams and work across Architecture, SRE, Service Assurance, and cross-functional network teams.

Experience working in an agency environment, familiarity with donor CRM platforms and data visualization tools, and post-secondary education in marketing or a related field would be considered assets.

At Blue North, the work we do matters.

jobs.description:
Xplore Inc. is Canada’s fibre, 5G and satellite broadband company for rural living. Xplore is committed to the relentless pursuit of an improved broadband experience for all Canadians. Xplore is building a world-class fibre optic and 5G wireless network to enable innovative broadband services for better every day rural living, for today and future generations.

The Director, Network Development & Operations is the senior leader responsible for turning Xplore’s network architecture into an automated, scalable production network, delivering Core & Transport Network Services at a Tier-1 Telco Gold Standard and ensuring uncompromising reliability, security, and performance from the core to the customer. The role leads the teams accountable for detailed IP engineering, DWDM engineering automation, caching implementation, CI/CD, configuration management, telemetry, and operational tooling.

The Director sets the vision and operating model for network-as-code, ensuring that all IP/MPLS, DWDM, and caching configurations are deployed safely, consistently, and at scale. Under this leadership, the organization builds the automation frameworks, observability pipelines, and operational guardrails that enable high-velocity, low-risk changes across the backbone, reduce manual toil, and strengthen 24×7 operational readiness.

Working in close partnership with Network Architecture & Technology Strategy, the Director ensures that architectural intent is executed through modern DevOps practices, and brings operational insight back into standards, roadmaps, and long-term network evolution. The Director connects network development and operations directly to business outcomes and KPIs — including reliability, speed of change, customer experience, and cost efficiency — and serves as a trusted advisor to senior leadership on operational performance and automation maturity.

Key Responsibilities Include

Detailed IP, DWDM & Caching Engineering

Own detailed IP engineering across BGP, OSPF, IS-IS, MPLS, segment routing, and routing policy.
Own DWDM configuration automation, including line-system configuration templates, channel provisioning, amplifier and span parameter automation, optical telemetry integration, and operational tooling for DWDM health and performance.
Own caching platform implementation, including cache node configuration, routing and traffic-steering policies, cache peering and placement logic (as defined by Architecture), and performance tuning and hit-ratio optimization.
Translate architectural standards into deployable configuration templates and network-as-code artifacts.

Network Automation & CI/CD Pipelines

Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for IP/MPLS/DWDM and caching configuration deployment.
Implement automated testing, validation, and rollback capabilities.
Drive adoption of network-as-code across the Core & Transport domain, ensuring all changes are executed through automated, repeatable workflows.

Telemetry, Observability & Operational Tooling

jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Anthropic is building AI systems that will shape the trajectory of one of the most consequential technologies in human history. That work requires physical infrastructure at significant scale, and building that infrastructure the right way means being a real, long-term partner to the communities where we operate.

We are looking for a Community Engagement Manager in Canada to join our Public Policy team and serve as Anthropic's on-the-ground presence in the communities where our data centres are sited, built, and operated. This role sits where community engagement, government relations and public affairs meet, and you may come from any of them. What matters is that you know how decisions get made in Alberta and can earn trust in a county council chamber, a minister's office or a community hall. Your job is to make Anthropic a trusted, visible, and valued neighbour, from the earliest stages of site selection through construction and long-term operations.

You will be the connective tissue between Anthropic's Policy and Infrastructure teams and the local officials, community organizations, economic development partners, and residents who have a stake in what we build. You will surface concerns before they escalate, translate our technical and operational plans into clear local benefits, and build the coalitions that allow us to move quickly and responsibly. Because Anthropic's infrastructure footprint is still early in its growth, you will also help write the playbook: the processes you build in your first markets are the ones we will use as we expand.

You will travel regularly within Alberta, up to 50% of the time, and occasionally to other Anthropic data centre markets. We will also consider applicants based in Ottawa who have established professional experience or relationships relevant to Alberta and can spend at least half their time in the province.

Key responsibilities

Build and maintain trusted, sustained relationships with municipal governments, both elected and unelected, MLAs, provincial ministers and agencies, economic development organizations, community groups, civic leaders, educational institutions, and workforce partners in the data centre markets you cover
Engage respectfully and meaningfully with Indigenous communities, including First Nations, Metis Settlements, and Métis governments and organizations, building sustained relationships and supporting consultation and partnership efforts related to our projects
Support projects through local decisions such as development permits and public hearings, working closely with our development partners and their community and Indigenous relations teams
Develop and execute a community engagement strategy for each of your markets, spanning site selection, pre-development, construction, and ongoing operations
Build external coalitions, host education and listening sessions, and design local solutions that deliver real benefits to the communities where we operate
Represent Anthropic in public forums, town halls, planning hearings, community events, and local media
Monitor community sentiment and local and provincial political dynamics, and advise internal teams on risks, opportunities, and the right pace and posture for engagement
Partner with the Real Estate and Infrastructure team to bring community input into how projects are planned, communicated, and delivered, not just how they are announced
Work with Communications and Policy colleagues on public affairs in Alberta, including local media, advertising and trusted third-party voices
Coordinate charitable giving, community investment, and economic development commitments in your markets, including managing nonprofit partner relationships and helping show what that investment delivers
Partner with the Energy and Sustainability team to explain our approach to environmental stewardship and respond to questions about power, water, and land use
Work with colleagues in Alberta to build a playbook and repeatable processes that scale as Anthropic's infrastructure footprint grows

Minimum Qualifications

Experience in government relations, public affairs, political or government staff roles, community affairs, economic development, or a closely related field
Direct experience working in or with Alberta's municipal or provincial governments, and a working understanding of how local and provincial politics and community dynamics actually play out
A skilled relationship and coalition builder who earns trust with a diverse group of stakeholders, and who maintains relationships through difficult conversations
The ability to represent a company credibly in public settings, including town halls, hearings, and press interviews
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn a complex operational plan into plain language that a local official or reporter can understand and respond to
The ability to work independently, get up to speed quickly on complex policy issues, and manage multiple concurrent engagements across different markets without losing track of any of them
Based in Alberta or willing to relocate there, and prepared to travel regularly across the province. We will also consider applicants based in Ottawa who have established professional experience or relationships relevant to Alberta, on the understanding that they will travel to Alberta at least half the time

Preferred Qualifications

7+ years of experience in government relations, public affairs, or community engagement, ideally including energy, utility, or large-scale industrial infrastructure projects
Experience as political staff or in a senior government role in Alberta, at the municipal, provincial, or federal level
Experience on a public affairs campaign that combined stakeholder outreach with earned or paid media
Familiarity with land use, zoning, and development permitting processes at the municipal and provincial level
Experience managing corporate social responsibility programs
Established relationships with economic development, workforce, or civic organizations in the markets this role covers
Experience working with real estate, legal, communications, and policy teams at the same time
Experience working with Indigenous communities in Canada, including familiarity with consultation processes, Indigenous rights and treaty considerations, or community benefit and partnership agreements
A genuine interest in the communities where you work, not just the projects you are managing

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California:
We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

POSITION DESCRIPTION

The Director of Finance is a senior finance leader responsible for the integrity, stewardship, and governance of ESA’s financial operations and financial reporting. Financial Accounting and Reporting

· Provide financial and accounting leadership for ESA’s Finance function and business areas. Oversee all accounts, ledgers, and reporting systems and changes thereto, ensuring continued compliance with appropriate GAAP standards and regulatory requirements.
· Design and maintain internal controls and safeguards related to revenue (billings and receipts) and expenditures.
· Oversee the preparation and integrity of monthly, quarterly and annual financial reports in accordance with GAAP.
· Lead the month end and year end close processes, ensuring timeliness, completeness, and accuracy.
· Lead the annual ESA external financial statement audit, including planning, fieldwork and reporting while keeping the CFO apprised of any issues on a timely basis.

Internal Controls, Compliance and Audit

· Design, implement, and maintain a strong internal control framework over financial reporting.
· Ensure compliance with statutory, regulatory, tax, and reporting requirements.
· Act as the primary liaison with external auditors, regulators, and other external stakeholders on accounting and control matters.

· Identify, assess, and mitigate financial reporting and operational financial risks.

· Establish and monitor key controls over disbursements, collections, credit management, and reconciliations.

Treasury, Cash Management & Banking

Other

understanding of GAAP and accounting for pensions.

new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Anthropic is building AI systems that will shape the trajectory of one of the most consequential technologies in human history. That work requires physical infrastructure at significant scale, and building that infrastructure the right way means being a real, long-term partner to the communities where we operate.

We are looking for a Community Engagement Manager in Canada to join our Public Policy team and serve as Anthropic's on-the-ground presence in the communities where our data centres are sited, built, and operated. This role sits where community engagement, government relations and public affairs meet, and you may come from any of them. What matters is that you know how decisions get made in Alberta and can earn trust in a county council chamber, a minister's office or a community hall. Your job is to make Anthropic a trusted, visible, and valued neighbour, from the earliest stages of site selection through construction and long-term operations.

You will be the connective tissue between Anthropic's Policy and Infrastructure teams and the local officials, community organizations, economic development partners, and residents who have a stake in what we build. You will surface concerns before they escalate, translate our technical and operational plans into clear local benefits, and build the coalitions that allow us to move quickly and responsibly. Because Anthropic's infrastructure footprint is still early in its growth, you will also help write the playbook: the processes you build in your first markets are the ones we will use as we expand.

You will travel regularly within Alberta, up to 50% of the time, and occasionally to other Anthropic data centre markets. We will also consider applicants based in Ottawa who have established professional experience or relationships relevant to Alberta and can spend at least half their time in the province.

Key responsibilities

Build and maintain trusted, sustained relationships with municipal governments, both elected and unelected, MLAs, provincial ministers and agencies, economic development organizations, community groups, civic leaders, educational institutions, and workforce partners in the data centre markets you cover
Engage respectfully and meaningfully with Indigenous communities, including First Nations, Metis Settlements, and Métis governments and organizations, building sustained relationships and supporting consultation and partnership efforts related to our projects
Support projects through local decisions such as development permits and public hearings, working closely with our development partners and their community and Indigenous relations teams
Develop and execute a community engagement strategy for each of your markets, spanning site selection, pre-development, construction, and ongoing operations
Build external coalitions, host education and listening sessions, and design local solutions that deliver real benefits to the communities where we operate
Represent Anthropic in public forums, town halls, planning hearings, community events, and local media
Monitor community sentiment and local and provincial political dynamics, and advise internal teams on risks, opportunities, and the right pace and posture for engagement
Partner with the Real Estate and Infrastructure team to bring community input into how projects are planned, communicated, and delivered, not just how they are announced
Work with Communications and Policy colleagues on public affairs in Alberta, including local media, advertising and trusted third-party voices
Coordinate charitable giving, community investment, and economic development commitments in your markets, including managing nonprofit partner relationships and helping show what that investment delivers
Partner with the Energy and Sustainability team to explain our approach to environmental stewardship and respond to questions about power, water, and land use
Work with colleagues in Alberta to build a playbook and repeatable processes that scale as Anthropic's infrastructure footprint grows

Minimum Qualifications

Experience in government relations, public affairs, political or government staff roles, community affairs, economic development, or a closely related field
Direct experience working in or with Alberta's municipal or provincial governments, and a working understanding of how local and provincial politics and community dynamics actually play out
A skilled relationship and coalition builder who earns trust with a diverse group of stakeholders, and who maintains relationships through difficult conversations
The ability to represent a company credibly in public settings, including town halls, hearings, and press interviews
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn a complex operational plan into plain language that a local official or reporter can understand and respond to
The ability to work independently, get up to speed quickly on complex policy issues, and manage multiple concurrent engagements across different markets without losing track of any of them
Based in Alberta or willing to relocate there, and prepared to travel regularly across the province. We will also consider applicants based in Ottawa who have established professional experience or relationships relevant to Alberta, on the understanding that they will travel to Alberta at least half the time

Preferred Qualifications

7+ years of experience in government relations, public affairs, or community engagement, ideally including energy, utility, or large-scale industrial infrastructure projects
Experience as political staff or in a senior government role in Alberta, at the municipal, provincial, or federal level
Experience on a public affairs campaign that combined stakeholder outreach with earned or paid media
Familiarity with land use, zoning, and development permitting processes at the municipal and provincial level
Experience managing corporate social responsibility programs
Established relationships with economic development, workforce, or civic organizations in the markets this role covers
Experience working with real estate, legal, communications, and policy teams at the same time
Experience working with Indigenous communities in Canada, including familiarity with consultation processes, Indigenous rights and treaty considerations, or community benefit and partnership agreements
A genuine interest in the communities where you work, not just the projects you are managing

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California:
We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.
